question: How many times does a GPS satellite circle the earth?
solution:
The correct answer is "**Once every 12 hours".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• GPS satellite blocks are various output generations of the **Global Positioning System** "GPS". accustomed for satellite navigation.
 
• The system's first satellite, his** Navstar 1**, was launched on **February 22, 1978**.
 
• The GPS satellite constellation is operated by Space Delta 8's 2nd Space Operations Squadron (2 SOPS), United States Space Force.
 
• GPS satellites orbit the Earth at an altitude of about **20,000 km (12,427 miles),** making two complete orbits each day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navstar** is the US satellite network that provides the **Global Positioning System "GPS"**. service.
 
• They are used for navigation by both military and civilians.
 
• These** 24** major GPS satellites orbit the earth every **12 hours**, broadcasting synchronization signals from each satellite.
